places.summary: Small town at Madeira's north-west tip, famous for lava-rock sea pools. A quiet overnight base for the west and the north coast.
facts: About 55 min from Funchal via the expressway
Several hotels and guesthouses by the pools
Good stop on a north coast loop with Seixal and São Vicente

places.name: Porto Moniz natural pools
places.summary: Natural swimming pools formed in black volcanic rock, refilled by Atlantic waves crashing over the edge. The managed complex has lifeguards, changing rooms and sunbeds.
facts: ~€3 adult
Free wild pools nearby too
Bring water shoes; rock is sharp
Opening hours shorter in winter
places.season: Sea water about 18–20 °C in autumn; pools may close in big swells.

places.name: Seixal black sand beach
places.summary: Small beach of black volcanic sand framed by green cliffs and waterfalls, one of the most photogenic spots on the north coast. Seixal also has natural rock pools.
facts: Free; small car park
Showers and a beach bar in summer
Combine with Porto Moniz
Water entry is steep with waves
places.caution: Strong waves and currents on the north coast; swim only in calm conditions.

places.name: Fanal forest
places.summary: Upland meadow at about 1,100 m dotted with gnarled centuries-old laurel (til) trees, often wrapped in drifting fog. Short, easy walking and very atmospheric.
facts: Free; roadside parking off the ER209
Fog makes the best photos — go in the morning
Cows graze freely
About 25 min uphill from Porto Moniz
places.season: Can be cold and wet; fog almost guaranteed outside summer.

places.name: 25 Fontes & Risco levada walk (PR6)
places.summary: From Rabaçal on the Paul da Serra plateau, levadas lead down through laurel forest to the Risco waterfall and the 25 Fontes basin where dozens of springs spill down a mossy wall.
facts: About 11 km return, 3–4 h
Park on the ER110 and walk or take the shuttle (~€3–5) down to Rabaçal
Very popular — start early
PR trail registration fee may apply (~€3)
places.caution: Narrow, crowded path with drops; can be closed after storms.

places.name: Calheta
places.summary: Sunny south-west town with a marina, a sheltered golden sand beach (imported) and the MUDAS contemporary art museum. A good base for the west, Rabaçal levadas and sunset.
facts: Calm sheltered swimming at the man-made beach
MUDAS museum on the cliff above
About 35 min from Funchal
Several resorts and guesthouses

places.name: Ponta do Sol
places.summary: Small seaside village with a pebble beach, waterfront cafés and Madeira's sunniest climate; now home to a digital nomad community.
facts: Free; small parking near the seafront
Good sunset stop
Combine with Calheta and Cabo Girão

places.name: Eira do Serrado viewpoint
places.summary: Viewpoint at about 1,000 m looking straight down into the deep crater-like valley of Curral das Freiras. A trail descends to the village below.
facts: Free parking, café and shop at the top
About 25 min from Funchal
Walk down to Curral das Freiras (~1 h) and take the bus back
places.caution: Valley is often filled with cloud by midday.

places.name: Curral das Freiras (Nun's Valley)
places.summary: Village deep in a steep mountain bowl where nuns once fled pirates. Known for chestnut liqueur and cakes and for dramatic views up to the encircling peaks.
facts: Free; reached by tunnel road
Try chestnut liqueur or cake
Combine with Eira do Serrado above

places.name: Porto Santo
places.summary: Madeira's small, dry sister island with a 9 km golden sand beach, unlike anything on Madeira itself. Vila Baleira has the house where Columbus is said to have lived.
facts: Ferry from Funchal about 2.5 h each way, or a 15-min flight
Good as a day trip or 1–2 nights
Rent a bike or car to see the viewpoints
Very quiet outside summer
places.season: Ferry runs most days; sea can be rough in winter.

places.name: Ponta Delgada Airport (PDL)
places.summary: São Miguel's main airport, a few minutes west of Ponta Delgada. Hub for SATA/Azores Airlines inter-island and mainland flights.
facts: Taxi to the centre ~€10
Car hire desks in arrivals — book ahead
Inter-island flights by SATA Air Açores

places.name: Terceira Lajes Airport (TER)
places.summary: Shared civil-military airport on Terceira's north-east coast, about 25 minutes from Angra do Heroísmo.
facts: Taxi to Angra ~€25
Car hire in arrivals
Bus to Angra and Praia da Vitória

places.name: Horta Airport (HOR)
places.summary: Faial's small airport at Castelo Branco, about 10 km west of Horta.
facts: Taxi to Horta ~€12–15
Limited car hire — book ahead
Ferries to Pico leave from Horta harbour

places.name: Ponta Delgada
places.summary: The Azores' largest town, on São Miguel's south coast, with black-and-white basalt streets, the triple-arched city gates and a long marina promenade. Main base for the island and for whale watching.
facts: Best base for São Miguel; most tours start here
Visit a pineapple greenhouse (Arruda) on the edge of town
Street parking is metered; use garages
Lively seafront in the evening
places.season: Mild but changeable (16–21 °C in autumn); expect showers and fast-moving cloud.

places.name: Whale watching from Ponta Delgada
places.summary: Boat trips (RIB or catamaran) guided by lookouts on shore, with very high chances of dolphins and good chances of sperm whales year-round; blue and fin whales pass in spring.
facts: ~€60–70 adult for about 3 h
Book ahead; trips are cancelled in rough seas
RIBs are faster but wetter; catamarans better for kids
Morning trips usually calmer
places.season: Spring (Apr–May) is best for baleen whales; winter trips are often cancelled for weather.

places.name: Sete Cidades & Vista do Rei
places.summary: A huge volcanic caldera holding the twin Blue and Green lakes, seen best from the Vista do Rei viewpoint on the rim. Below, the village of Sete Cidades sits on the lake shore.
facts: Free; parking at Vista do Rei
Also see Boca do Inferno viewpoint (short walk) and Lagoa do Canário
Rim walk along the caldera is a fine half-day hike
Check webcams (SpotAzores) — it is often in cloud
places.caution: Cloud often fills the crater; come back later in the day if it is fogged in.

places.name: Mosteiros
places.summary: Fishing village at São Miguel's western tip with a black sand beach, lava rock pools and sea stacks just offshore. One of the island's best sunset spots.
facts: Free parking near the beach
Natural pools for swimming in calm weather
Combine with Sete Cidades and Ferraria
places.caution: Strong currents off the beach; swim in the pools.

places.name: Ponta da Ferraria thermal pool
places.summary: A natural ocean pool in a lava cove where hot spring water mixes with the Atlantic, with ropes to hold on to. Best around low tide when the water is warmest.
facts: Sea pool is free; a spa building next door is ticketed
Go at low tide — check a tide table
Steep road down; parking at the end
Water shoes help
places.caution: Waves surge in with force; hold the ropes and stay out in big swells.

places.name: Lagoa do Fogo
places.summary: Crater lake in the middle of São Miguel surrounded by wild, untouched slopes and a white sand shore. Viewpoints on the road, or hike down to the water.
facts: Free; viewpoint parking on the EN5-2A
Trail down to the lake ~1 h each way
Access road sometimes limited in summer peak (shuttle)
Often in cloud — check webcams
places.caution: Fog can roll in within minutes on the mountain road.

places.name: Caldeira Velha
places.summary: Small nature park in a fern-filled ravine with a warm iron-rich waterfall pool and hotter thermal pools. Feels like a jungle.
facts: ~€10 to bathe, less for a visit only
Time slots; book ahead in summer
Changing rooms on site
Iron-rich water stains light swimwear

places.name: Gorreana Tea Plantation
places.summary: Europe's oldest continuously operating tea plantation, founded in 1883, on the north coast. You can see the old machinery at work, taste free tea and walk among the bushes.
facts: Free entry and tasting
Short walking trails through the plantation
Shop sells local black and green tea
Porto Formoso plantation is nearby too

places.name: Furnas
places.summary: Spa village in a volcanic valley full of steaming fumaroles and mineral springs. Home to the Terra Nostra garden, Poça da Dona Beija and the famous cozido stew cooked in the ground.
facts: Good overnight base — soak in hot springs after dark
Try cozido das Furnas at lunch; book a table
Caldeiras with boiling mud in the village centre
About 45 min from Ponta Delgada

places.name: Furnas Lake & caldeiras
places.summary: Crater lake whose north shore steams with fumaroles where pots of cozido are buried in the ground to cook for about six hours. Watch them being lifted out around noon.
facts: Small parking/entry fee to the fumarole area
Cozido pots come out about 12:00–13:00
Walking path around the lake (~9 km)
Gruta do Padre José Jacinto chapel on the shore

places.name: Terra Nostra Garden
places.summary: 18th-century botanical garden in Furnas with an enormous yellow-brown iron-rich thermal pool at about 35–40 °C, plus camellias, ferns and cycads.
facts: ~€10–15 adult; bathing included
Wear an old dark swimsuit — water stains
Showers and changing rooms; pool busy at midday
Evening hours in summer

places.name: Poça da Dona Beija
places.summary: Set of small, lantern-lit thermal pools beside a stream in Furnas, open late into the evening. Great after a day of sightseeing.
facts: ~€8 adult
Lockers and showers
Open into the late evening
Queues at peak times

places.name: Salto do Prego waterfall hike
places.summary: Loop trail from the village of Faial da Terra through a lush valley to a 20 m waterfall, passing the restored hamlet of Sanguinho.
facts: About 4.5 km loop, 2 h
Free; parking in Faial da Terra
Moderate with some steep, slippery stretches
Swimming possible in the pool below the fall
places.season: Waterfall strongest after autumn/winter rain.

places.name: Nordeste viewpoints & Ponta do Sossego
places.summary: Manicured flower-filled viewpoint gardens perched above the cliffs of the remote north-east, with Ponta da Madrugada a few minutes away — a sunrise favourite.
facts: Free; picnic tables and toilets
Ponta da Madrugada nearby for sunrise
Combine with Salto do Prego and Furnas
Roads are winding: allow time

places.name: Angra do Heroísmo
places.summary: UNESCO-listed Renaissance port town on Terceira with a grid of pastel streets, imperial chapels (impérios) and forts guarding the bay. The most elegant town in the Azores.
facts: Climb the Alto da Memória obelisk for the view
Museu de Angra do Heroísmo in a former convent
Lively during the summer Sanjoaninas festival
Good base for all of Terceira

places.name: Monte Brasil
places.summary: Volcanic peninsula beside Angra wrapped by the walls of the São João Baptista fortress, with forest trails and viewpoints over the town and bay.
facts: Free; trails start from the fortress or park
Loop around 7 km, about 2 h
Pico das Cruzinhas viewpoint by car

places.name: Algar do Carvão
places.summary: A rare open lava tube: you descend into the empty throat of an extinct volcano, past mossy walls and stalactites of silica, to a clear rain-fed lake at the bottom.
facts: ~€10 adult; combined ticket with Gruta do Natal available
Limited opening outside summer — check before going
Steep steps, can be wet
Bring a jacket: cool and damp inside
places.season: Opening days and hours are reduced from autumn to spring.

places.name: Serra do Cume viewpoint
places.summary: Ridge viewpoint over Terceira's patchwork quilt of green fields divided by stone walls, stretching to Praia da Vitória and the sea.
facts: Free; parking at the top
Late afternoon light is best
Close to Lajes airport — easy first or last stop

places.name: Biscoitos natural pools
places.summary: Swimming pools in black lava rock on Terceira's north coast, with ladders and sunbathing terraces. The village also has a small wine museum and vineyards in lava-stone pens.
facts: Free; changing rooms in summer
Biscoitos wine museum nearby
Best on calm, sunny days
places.season: Swimming mainly June–October; rough seas in winter.

places.name: Horta
places.summary: Faial's harbour town, a historic stop for transatlantic sailors, whose marina walls are covered with crews' painted logos. Views across the channel to Mount Pico.
facts: Have a gin at Peter Café Sport
Ferry to Madalena (Pico) from the harbour
Monte da Guia viewpoint just south
Good base for Faial and Pico

places.name: Capelinhos Volcano
places.summary: Moonscape of ash and cinder left by the 1957–58 eruption that added land to Faial's western tip, with a half-buried lighthouse and an excellent underground interpretation centre.
facts: Interpretation centre ~€10; lighthouse climb included
Walk up the ash cone for views
About 30 min from Horta
Windy and exposed
places.caution: Stay on paths; ash slopes are loose and cliffs unstable.

places.name: Caldeira do Faial
places.summary: A 2 km-wide, 400 m-deep volcanic crater at the centre of Faial, with a rim trail and views over the island and Pico.
facts: Free; parking at the end of the road
Short tunnel walk to the rim viewpoint
Rim loop ~7 km, 2.5 h
Often in cloud
places.caution: Rim trail is exposed and windy; turn back in fog.

places.name: Madalena (Pico)
places.summary: Pico's main ferry port and small town, facing Faial across the channel. A convenient base for climbing Mount Pico and visiting the vineyards.
facts: Ferry to Horta about 30 min
Car hire near the port — book ahead
Wine co-operative shop in town

places.name: Pico vineyards (UNESCO)
places.wiki: Landscape of the Pico Island Vineyard Culture
places.summary: A grid of thousands of small stone-walled pens (currais) built of black lava to protect vines from wind and salt, best seen at Criação Velha and Lajido. Verdelho wine was once exported to the tsars.
facts: Free to walk; Pico Wine Museum in Madalena
Tastings at local wineries
Combine with the Madalena coast walk

places.name: Mount Pico climb
places.summary: Portugal's highest mountain (2,351 m), a steep volcanic cone climbed from the Casa da Montanha at 1,200 m. The summit crater and the tiny Piquinho peak give views over the whole central group.
facts: Registration at Casa da Montanha required, fee ~€20–25; GPS tracker issued
7–8 h return; very steep, loose scree
Guide recommended; start early
Check weather — climbs are restricted in bad conditions
places.caution: Serious mountain: sudden fog, cold and wind; many rescues every year.
places.season: Winter climbs can have snow and ice and may be closed.

places.name: Caminho do Mar (Via Ferrata dos Pinheirinhos)
places.summary: A short but airy coastal via ferrata on the limestone cliffs west of Sesimbra, with the ocean directly below. The equipment is sparse and the approach is tricky to find, so it suits people who already have some experience.
facts: Grade K3 (RocJumper) / C/D (ferrataguide, via-ferrata.de) · 430 m · +223 m · ~2 h 25 min in total

Getting there: Drive from Sesimbra toward Zambujal de Cima, then along Rua dos Almocreves to a small parking area. Walk dirt tracks toward the sea, then descend to the cliff with the help of fixed ropes. Allow 40–45 min.
Total about 2 h 25 min: 40 min approach, 1 h on the route, 45 min back
Length disagrees: 430 m equipped (RocJumper, 2025) vs 800 m (ferrataguide)
The approach descends steeply with fixed ropes; a GPS track helps
The route starts near Praia do Ribeiro do Cavalo
On the route: Sea-cliff traverse above the Atlantic, very exposed, sparsely equipped, fixed ropes on the approach, sea views throughout
Access: Free to self-guide; guided trips from about €45–65
Operator: No managing body found; guided by Vertente Natural (vertentenatural.com) and sold via Manawa
Kit: Vertente Natural includes harness and helmet in the trip price; no standalone rental found
Bring helmet, harness and a via ferrata lanyard set (EN 958); turn back in rain, wind or very high fire risk
places.season: Operators run it year-round; no official closure periods found

places.name: Caminho sobre o Oceano Ordovícico (Via Ferrata da Serra do Muradal)
places.summary: Portugal's second via ferrata (2015), a short, staple-only climb on quartzite ridges in the Naturtejo Geopark. It's a good first via ferrata, and the views over the ancient folded ridges are the highlight.
facts: Grade K2 (RocJumper 2025) / A/B (via-ferrata.de); officially 'algo difícil' (≈K3); OSM says B · 211 m · +150 m · ~2 h 00 min in total

Getting there: From the EN238 near Estreito, take the dirt road signed 'Parque eólico do Pinhal Interior' to a saddle with an info panel. Follow the GR38 path to the base of the rock, about 10–20 min.
About 2 h total: 20 min approach, 1.5 h route, 10 min back
Grade sources disagree, from A/B to K3; most recent (RocJumper 2025) says K2
Height: 75–90 m equipped, about 150 m total ascent including approach
No warning signs at the start, so put your helmet on during the approach
On the route: Staples on quartzite ridges, no bridges, wide views over the Muradal crest, part of the GR38 Pangeia route
Access: Free; guided €80 with Epic Land
Operator: Município de Oleiros with Naturtejo Geopark; guided trips by Epic Land (epicland.pt, bookable via bookinxisto.com)
Kit: Epic Land includes equipment in its €80 trip; no standalone rental found
Bring helmet, harness and a via ferrata lanyard set (EN 958); turn back in rain, wind or very high fire risk
places.season: All year (Caminhantes); the area burned some years ago and is regrowing

places.name: Via Ferrata da Serra das Talhadas
places.summary: The longest via ferrata in Portugal, a ridge circuit with two bridges in the Naturtejo Geopark. It reopened in 2026 after repairs from the 2023 wildfires.
facts: We've done this one: E29 / CJE via ferrata activity (2021)
Grade K3 (RocJumper) / B/C (ferrataguide, via-ferrata.de) · 2190 m · +150 m · ~2 h 21 min in total

Getting there: From Catraia Cimeira take the M1313 toward Chão do Galego. Start at the watchtower designed by Álvaro Siza Vieira, then walk about 800 m (20 min) to sector 1. The circuit ends back at the tower.
Reopened mid-2026 after fire damage; it was listed as temporarily closed before that
Length disagrees: 2,190 m total (municipality) vs 1,400 m (2021 press)
The municipality recommends going with experience or with a guide
One person at a time on the Himalayan bridge, two on the suspension bridge
On the route: Circular traverse in 11 sectors, a 15 m Himalayan bridge, a 40 m suspension bridge, ladders, views over the Ocreza valley
Access: Free
Operator: Município de Proença-a-Nova; guided trips by Epic Land (epicland.pt)
Kit: Epic Land includes equipment in its guided trips; no standalone rental found
Bring helmet, harness and a via ferrata lanyard set (EN 958); turn back in rain, wind or very high fire risk
places.season: The municipality says not to use it in bad weather or at very high fire risk

places.name: Via Ferrata do Rabaçal (Ecovia do Rabaçal)
places.summary: The only via ferrata in Trás-os-Montes, climbing a granite slope above the wild Rabaçal river, with an optional cable bridge at the top. It pairs well with the Ecovia walking trails and the river beach.
facts: We've done this one: E29 / CJE via ferrata activity (2024)
Grade K2 (deandar) / B (via-ferrata.de, OSM); officially 'algo difícil' ≈K3 · 120 m · +95 m · ~2 h 15 min in total

Getting there: Park on Rua Principal in Barreiros, by the cemetery and festival square. Walk down past a viewpoint to the river beach, then follow signs to the panel at the start. The loop is about 4.4 km.
Circular walk about 2 h 15 min in total (Wikiloc track)
Grade sources disagree, from K2 to K3; the steepest section is slightly overhanging
Opened in 2019–2020 as part of the Ecovia do Rabaçal
Barreiros is 16 km from Valpaços and about 22 km from Chaves
On the route: Granite wall above the Rabaçal river, a slightly overhanging section, an optional Tibetan/Himalayan bridge (~20 m) at the end, a river beach nearby
Access: Free; guided €30
Operator: Município de Valpaços; guided trips by Azibeiro House Nature (€30, minimum 3 people)
Kit: Azibeiro includes PPE in its €30 trip; no standalone rental found
Bring helmet, harness and a via ferrata lanyard set (EN 958); turn back in rain, wind or very high fire risk
places.season: No official closures found

places.name: Via Ferrata do Barranco do Demo
places.summary: A short, very easy via ferrata from 2025, built off the Barranco do Demo walkways near Alferce. It makes a good family add-on to the walkway hike.
facts: Grade K1 (RocJumper) / A (ferrataguide); a Wikiloc user rates it a very easy K2 · 300 m · +35 m · ~0 h 40 min in total
Getting there: Drive to Alferce and follow signs to the Passadiços do Barranco do Demo; parking is near the cemetery. The via ferrata starts off the walkways, about 5 min away.
About 30 min on the route plus 5 min each way
No managing body, fee, or kit rental found; check with Câmara de Monchique
Opened 2025 (Wikiloc track description)
On the route: A small suspension bridge, handrails, gorge views, combines with the walkways and their 50 m suspension bridge
Access: Unknown; the walkways are free to visit
Bring helmet, harness and a via ferrata lanyard set (EN 958); turn back in rain, wind or very high fire risk

places.name: Via Ferrata da Penha (Senhora da Penha)
places.summary: A short beginner route built in 2015 up the cliff below the Penha hermitage, with wide views over Castelo de Vide. The sideways traverses are the most technical part.
facts: We've done this one: E29 / CJE via ferrata activity (2024)
Grade K2 (RocJumper) / B (via-ferrata.de) · 200 m · +54 m · ~0 h 45 min in total
Getting there: Park at the Ermida de Nossa Senhora da Penha car park above Castelo de Vide. Follow yellow dots downhill to the base of the cliff, about 10 min. Return by the chapel stairs.
About 45 min: 10 min approach, 30 min climb, 5 min back
Length disagrees: 160 m (RocJumper) vs 200 m (via-ferrata.de, Caminhantes)
Third via ferrata built in Portugal
GreenRoc minimum age is 14
On the route: Gneiss cliff, a short negatively-sloping traverse, views over Castelo de Vide, finishes at the hermitage
Access: Free
Operator: Câmara Municipal de Castelo de Vide with CIMAA (Alentejo Feel Nature); guided trips by GreenRoc (greenroc.pt) and via GetYourGuide
Kit: Guided trips include equipment; no standalone rental or price found
Bring helmet, harness and a via ferrata lanyard set (EN 958); turn back in rain, wind or very high fire risk
places.season: All year (Caminhantes); the area was recently burned

places.name: Via Ferrata da Barragem de Santa Luzia
places.summary: Portugal's hardest via ferrata, a short but strenuous climb up the granite wall beside the Santa Luzia dam. It's for experienced people with good arm strength.
facts: Grade K4 (RocJumper, deandar) / D (ferrataguide) / C/D (via-ferrata.de) · 200 m · +150 m · ~1 h 32 min in total
Getting there: Park at the foot of the Santa Luzia dam (Casal da Lapa) and walk to the west wall, about 2 min. Return over the dam or via the viewpoint on the N344.
Duration disagrees: about 1.5 h total (RocJumper) vs about 2.5 h (ferrataguide)
Several overhanging sections make it strenuous; not for beginners
Go in the morning for shade
On the route: 5 sections, vertical slabs, several slightly overhanging passages, ledges, ladders, dam and reservoir views
Access: Free; guided from €90
Operator: Município de Pampilhosa da Serra with Aldeias do Xisto; guided trips by Epic Land
Kit: Epic Land guided trip from €90, equipment included
Bring helmet, harness and a via ferrata lanyard set (EN 958); turn back in rain, wind or very high fire risk
places.season: Shaded in the morning, in sun in the afternoon; no official closures found

places.name: Via Ferrata da Pombeira (Pombeira Adventure Park)
places.summary: Often called the most complete via ferrata in Portugal, it follows a granite gorge with waterfalls and crosses three cable bridges. The park was officially inaugurated in 2026 after years of delays.
facts: We've done this one: E29 / CJE via ferrata activity (2024)
Grade C (ferrataguide, viaferrata.pt); mostly B to B/C with a C finish · 750 m · +200 m · ~2 h 35 min in total
Getting there: Park at the Pombeira Adventure Park near Lamelas / Codeçais, then walk about 30 min to the start. The return to the car is short.
About 2.5 h: 30 min approach, 2 h route, 5 min back
Length disagrees: 750 m (operators) vs 1,560 m (ferrataguide)
It was closed to the public from late 2023 until the park's official opening in 2026
Bridge descriptions vary between sources
On the route: River-canyon route along the Pombeiro, three bridges (Himalayan/Tibetan/monkey, 9–40 m), waterfalls, ends at a suspended viewpoint
Access: Unknown whether the park charges entry; guided €25–70 depending on operator and group size
Operator: Município de Castro Daire (Pombeira Adventure Park); guided by Latitude 41, Zona Canyoning, GreenTrekker and others
Kit: Latitude 41 €55–70 with kit; Zona Canyoning €45; viaferrata.pt €35; GreenTrekker €25 without kit or €40 with
Bring helmet, harness and a via ferrata lanyard set (EN 958); turn back in rain, wind or very high fire risk
places.season: Very little shade, so avoid hot summer middays

places.name: Via Ferrata da Póvoa de Lanhoso (Monte do Pilar)
places.summary: Portugal's first via ferrata (2012), a short beginner climb up the country's largest granite monolith to Lanhoso castle. It is private, so you must book through DiverLanhoso.
facts: We've done this one: E29 / CJE via ferrata activity (2024)
Grade K2 officially, feels like K1 (ferrataguide) / A/B (via-ferrata.de) · 150 m · +55 m · ~0 h 31 min in total
Getting there: Drive up Rua do Pilar and park at the lower bend near the base of the monolith. The start is about 2 min away; walk down by road from the castle afterwards.
Signs at the start forbid using it without the operator
Directories report the cable isn't properly fixed at the anchors, and via-ferrata.de says it is no longer maintained
Length disagrees: 70 m (ferrataguide) vs 150 m (RocJumper, via-ferrata.de)
On the route: Granite monolith, staples, short traverses, ends at Lanhoso castle and the Pilar sanctuary; optional double abseil down
Access: Guided only (private); about €23–24 per person
Operator: DiverLanhoso (diverlanhoso.pt)
Kit: DiverLanhoso includes kit (via ferrata plus double abseil, €24)
Bring helmet, harness and a via ferrata lanyard set (EN 958); turn back in rain, wind or very high fire risk

places.name: Via Ferrata Teto do Mundo
places.summary: A short climb to a rocky summit viewpoint in the Barroso highlands, with a suspension bridge along the way. It's an easy add-on to a visit to the Barroso area.
facts: We've done this one: E29 / CJE via ferrata activity (2024)
Grade K3 (deandar) / C, mostly B (ferrataguide) · 153 m · +100 m · ~0 h 55 min in total
Getting there: Take the M520 southeast from the Alto Rabagão dam to the first farm, where a sign marks the access. Follow the fence and faint yellow arrows, about 10 min.
Status disagrees: listed as closed by Ferratas Hierro y Roca (2024), but RocJumper found it OK in 2025
Reopened by the municipality in March 2022 after fire damage to the bridge
Duration disagrees: about 55 min (RocJumper) vs about 80 min (ferrataguide)
On the route: Suspension bridge, ladders, rocky summit, viewpoint at the Teto do Mundo GIAHS observatory
Access: Free
Operator: Município de Boticas; guided outings have been run by Boticas Hotel Art & Spa and CEITA Montalegre
Bring helmet, harness and a via ferrata lanyard set (EN 958); turn back in rain, wind or very high fire risk
places.season: It closed briefly after a 2021–22 wildfire; no other closure info found

places.name: Lisbon Airport (LIS)
places.summary: Humberto Delgado airport, inside the city: 20–30 min to the centre by metro (red line) or taxi.
facts: Metro red line to the centre; change at Alameda or São Sebastião
Car rental desks in the P2 car park area
Allow 2 h before international flights in summer

places.name: Porto Airport (OPO)
places.summary: Francisco Sá Carneiro airport, ~25 min from central Porto by metro (line E, violet) or car.
facts: Metro line E to Trindade in ~30 min
Tolls: the A28/A4 near Porto are electronic-only in places

checklist: ID card (EU) or passport. Non-EU visitors: check the EES/ETIAS entry rules for the Schengen area.
Driving licence; credit card in the driver's name for the rental deposit.
Rental car with a Via Verde toll transponder (many motorways have electronic tolls only).
Book timed tickets ahead: Pena Palace, Livraria Lello, Jerónimos in high season, Benagil boat trips.
Many museums and monuments close on Mondays; some on public holidays (1 Jan, Easter, 1 May, 25 Dec).
Atlantic beaches: strong currents and big swell. Swim only at beaches with lifeguards and a green flag.
Cliffs (Algarve, Cabo da Roca, Nazaré): stay back from the edge, it can crumble.
Hiking in Madeira and the Azores: check the trail is open, start early, bring a rain jacket and a headlamp for tunnels.
Summer and early autumn: forest fire risk. No barbecues or open fires; follow road closures.
Lunch is usually 12:30–15:00 and dinner from 19:30; many restaurants close one day a week.
European Health Insurance Card (EU) or travel insurance.
